arxiv-2107-05769.title: Peabodies of Constant Width
arxiv-2107-05769.creator: Isaac Arelio, Luis Montejano, Deborah Oliveros
arxiv-2107-05769.description: Abstract 1. Introduction Bodies of constant width and their properties have been known for centuries. Leonard Euler, for example, studied them in the eighteenth century under the name of orbiforms. They have received considerable attention in popular mathematics, in such contexts as videos, surveys, devices, and art, among others.

arxiv-2205-06831.title: Aspects of Axions and ALPs Phenomenology
arxiv-2205-06831.creator: Maurizio Giannotti
arxiv-2205-06831.description: Abstract The physics of axions and axion-like particles (ALPs) is enjoying an incredibly productive period, with many new experimental proposals, theoretical idea, and original astrophysical and cosmological arguments which help the search effort. The large number of experimental proposals is likely to lead to fundamental advances (perhaps, a discovery?) in the coming years.

arxiv-2307-00548.title: Robust Target Localization in 2D: A Value-at-Risk Approach
arxiv-2307-00548.creator: João Domingos, João Xavier
arxiv-2307-00548.description: Abstract This paper consider considers the problem of locating a two dimensional target from range-measurements containing outliers. Assuming that the number of outlier is known, we formulate the problem of minimizing inlier losses while ignoring outliers. This leads to a combinatorial, non-convex, non-smooth problem involving the percentile function. Using the framework of risk analysis from Rockafellar et al.

arxiv-2310-18101.title: Radial velocities from Gaia BP/RP spectra
arxiv-2310-18101.creator: Sill Verberne ,, Sergey E. Koposov, Elena Maria Rossi, Tommaso Marchetti, Konrad Kuijken, Zephyr Penoyre
arxiv-2310-18101.description: Abstract Aims. The Gaia mission has provided us full astrometric solutions for over 1.5 1.5 B sources. However, only the brightest 34M of those have radial velocity measurements. As a proof of concept, this paper aims to close that gap, by obtaining radial velocity estimates from the low-resolution BP/RP spectra that Gaia now provides.

arxiv-2406-04498.title: Conformal Multi-Target Hyperrectangles
arxiv-2406-04498.creator: Max Sampson max-sampson@uiowa.edu, Kung-Sik Chan kung-sik-chan@uiowa.edu
arxiv-2406-04498.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Max Sampson max-sampson@uiowa.edu, Kung-Sik Chan kung-sik-chan@uiowa.edu. We propose conformal hyperrectangular prediction regions for multi-target regression. We propose split conformal prediction algorithms for both point and quantile regression to form hyperrectangular prediction regions, which allow for easy marginal interpretation and do not require covariance estimation. In practice, it is preferable that a prediction region is balanced, that is, having identical marginal prediction coverage, since prediction accuracy is generally equally important across components of the response vector.

arxiv-2407-05917.title: Unveiling nonmagnetic phase and many-body entanglement in two-dimensional random quantum magnets Sr 2 CuTe 1-x W x O 6
arxiv-2407-05917.creator: Dian Wu, Fan Yang, Giuseppe Carleo
arxiv-2407-05917.description: Abstract We apply a random-plaquette J 1 J_{1} - J 2 J_{2} model on the square lattice to capture the physics of a series of spin- 1 / 2 1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet compounds Sr 2 CuTe 1-x W x O 6 .

arxiv-2505-21084.title: Teleportation with non-maximally entangled states and underlying unitary algebras of certain bipartite systems
arxiv-2505-21084.creator: P. Dasgupta, D. Gangopadhyay
arxiv-2505-21084.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by P. Dasgupta, D. Gangopadhyay. New convenient thumbrules are obtained to test entanglement of wavefunctions for bipartite qubit and qutrit systems. All results are analytic. The new results are :(a)For bipartite qubit systems there exists a matrix A A for which D ​ e ​ t ​ A = 0 DetA=0 implies unentanglement while D ​ e ​ t ​ A ≠ 0 DetA\neq 0 implies entanglement. There is an underlying SU(2) algebra.

arxiv-2506-20703.title: Generative Blocks World: Moving Things Around in Pictures
arxiv-2506-20703.creator: Vaibhav Vavilala Seemandhar Jain Rahul Vasanth D.A. Forsyth Anand Bhattad
arxiv-2506-20703.description: Abstract We describe Generative Blocks World to interact with the scene of a generated image by manipulating simple geometric abstractions. Our method represents scenes as assemblies of convex 3D primitives, and the same scene can be represented by different numbers of primitives, allowing an editor to move either whole structures or small details.

arxiv-2507-04087.title: Forecasting the U.S. Renewable-Energy Mix with an ALR-BDARMA Compositional Time-Series Framework
arxiv-2507-04087.creator: Harrison Katz
arxiv-2507-04087.description: Abstract Accurate forecasts of the U.S. renewable‑generation mix are essential for planning transmission upgrades, sizing storage, and setting balancing‑market rules. We introduce a Bayesian Dirichlet ARMA model (BDARMA) tailored to monthly shares of hydro, geothermal, solar, wind, wood, municipal waste, and biofuels from January 2010 through January 2025.

arxiv-2507-05211.title: All in One: Visual-Description-Guided Unified Point Cloud Segmentation
arxiv-2507-05211.creator: Zongyan Han, Mohamed El Amine Boudjoghra, Jiahua Dong, Jinhong Wang, Rao Muhammad Anwer
arxiv-2507-05211.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zongyan Han, Mohamed El Amine Boudjoghra, Jiahua Dong, Jinhong Wang, Rao Muhammad Anwer. Unified segmentation of 3D point clouds is crucial for scene understanding, but is hindered by its sparse structure, limited annotations, and the challenge of distinguishing fine-grained object classes in complex environments. Existing methods often struggle to capture rich semantic and contextual information due to limited supervision and a lack of diverse multimodal cues, leading to suboptimal differentiation of classes and instances.

arxiv-2507-16440.title: Measuring the Unmeasurable? Systematic Evidence on Scale Transformations in Subjective Survey Data Department of Behavioural and Cognitive Science, University of Luxembourg. We thank Dan Benjamin, Anita Braga, Matthew Cashman, Elena Fumagalli, Leonard Goff, Ori Heffetz, Martijn Hendricks, Richard He
arxiv-2507-16440.creator: Caspar Kaiser
arxiv-2507-16440.description: Abstract Economists routinely use survey measures of, for example, risk preferences, trust, political attitudes, or wellbeing. The literature generally treats numerical response categories as if they represent equal psychological intervals. We provide the first systematic test of this assumption, developing a general framework to quantify how easily results can be overturned when this linearity assumption is relaxed.

pmc-10655324.title: Combinative effects of akarkara root-derived metabolites on anti-inflammatory and anti-alzheimer key enzymes: integrating bioassay-guided fractionation, GC-MS analysis, and in silico studies
pmc-10655324.creator: Rana M. Ibrahim, Passent M. Abdel-Baki, Ghada F. Elmasry, Ahmed A. El-Rashedy, Nariman E. Mahdy
pmc-10655324.description: BackgroundAnacyclus pyrethrum L. (Akarkara root), a valuable Ayurvedic remedy, is reported to exhibit various pharmacological activities. Akarkara root was subjected to bioassay-guided fractionation, to isolate its active constituents and discover their potential bioactivities, followed by computational analysis.MethodsThe methanol extract and its fractions, methylene chloride, and butanol, were assessed for their antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticholinergic potentials.

pmc-11692720.title: DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, SLEEP, AND QUALITY OF LIFE IN ADULTS WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS
pmc-11692720.creator: Idiatou Diallo, Judy Bass, Rashelle Musci, Leslie Adams, Joseph Gallo, Adam Spira
pmc-11692720.description: Physical, mental, and sleep problems threaten well-being; however, there is limited research on the temporal connections of these issues. We investigated the longitudinal associations among depressive symptoms, sleep disturbances, and quality of life (QoL) among middle-aged and older adults (aged 50+) with diabetes, hypertension, and/or cardiovascular disease in the United States.

pmc-11714123.title: Novel small molecule agonist improves behavior deficits and synaptic plasticity in a model of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11714123.creator: Raj Amin, Ian Steinke, Fajar Wibowo, Sieun Yoo, Vishnu Suppiramaniam, Meenakshi Singh, Robert Rusty Arnold
pmc-11714123.description: BackgroundThe increased incidence of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) rate represent an unmet medical need and thus critical for the development of novel molecular therapeutics. Recent work focusing on patients with apoE4 alleles has highlighted the association of brain cholesterol dysregulation with elevated pathological burden and neurodegeneration.

pmc-13086839.title: High Entropy Alloys Database generated with Large Language Model
pmc-13086839.creator: Vladimir Chizhevskiy, Gordana Marković, Salah-eddine Benrazzouq, Uroš Cvelbar, Alexandre Nominé, Janez Zavašnik
pmc-13086839.description: High entropy alloys (HEAs) represent a promising area in materials science, but systematic analysis of the extensive literature remains a challenge. In this study, we used Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to analyze 4,625 scientific articles from a restricted corpus representing publisher-accessible literature, successfully identifying and characterizing 12,427 of different high entropy alloys.

pmc-13236571.title: The expanding role of protease therapeutics (2012–2026): from replacement therapies to immune system modulation and beyond
pmc-13236571.creator: Sage E. Nelson, Samantha G. Martinusen, Raymond Pho, Lawton F. Long, Carl A. Denard
pmc-13236571.description: Proteases are powerful therapeutic agents, offering unique advantages over conventional small molecules and biologics through their ability to directly and precisely cleave and (de)activate their protein targets. Since the early 1990s, FDA-approved protease therapeutics have served as replacement therapies for hematological disorders, as enzyme supplements for digestive disorders, and as treatments for neuromuscular disorders.

pmc-13261892.title: Imaging vocal fold medial surface vibration across chest, head, whistle, and creaky voice production using optical coherence tomography: A single subject study
pmc-13261892.creator: Zhaoyan Zhang, Anna Wisniowiecki, Melissa Treinkman, Bette Wo, Emma Glenane, Diego E. Razura, M. Eugenia Castro, Brian E. Applegate, Michael M. Johns
pmc-13261892.description: This single-subject study used optical coherence tomography to image medial surface vibratory patterns during the production of chest, head, whistle, and creaky voice. Chest and head registers differed in medial surface thickness, with the chest voice produced with thicker vocal folds, greater vibratory amplitude, and a larger vertical phase difference than the head voice and the other voice qualities.

pmc-13416113.title: Global landscape of cranial prosthesis policies for medical hair loss: a narrative review
pmc-13416113.creator: Angela Anaeme, Joey Lu, Caroline Mann
pmc-13416113.description: BackgroundCranial prostheses (CPs) provide indispensable cosmetic and emotional support for individuals with medical hair loss. However, access remains inconsistent due to variable reimbursement policies and unclear classification as medical vs. cosmetic devices.ObjectiveTo characterize global CP coverage frameworks and evaluate how each predominant healthcare system model structures CP access, reimbursement, and eligibility.

pmc-13485948.title: Correlation analysis of cyclosporine A trough concentration with hematological and biochemical parameters: a retrospective study in pediatric aplastic anemia
pmc-13485948.creator: Qian Xu, Xintong Mao, Yi Yun, Ling Liu
pmc-13485948.description: Aplastic anemia (AA) is a life-threatening pediatric hematological disorder requiring immunosuppressive therapy with cyclosporine A (CsA), which has a narrow therapeutic window and significant interindividual variability. The relationship between CsA trough concentration and routine laboratory markers in children remains poorly defined. This retrospective study enrolled 14 pediatric AA patients (70 paired samples) followed over 12 months.

pmc-13554321.title: A comprehensive longitudinal study quantifying the systemic effects associated with ovariectomy and high-dose corticosteroids in a sheep model of osteoporosis
pmc-13554321.creator: Katie T Bisazza, Brad B Nelson, Russell V Anthony, Laurie R Goodrich, Kirk C McGilvray, Jeremiah T Easley
pmc-13554321.description: BackgroundThe sheep is a common preclinical model for osteoporosis in humans and allows for robust longitudinal studies. Appropriate characterization of large animal models is necessary prior to selection for preclinical studies. We sought to comprehensively characterize the process of bone loss in a 12-month sheep model of osteoporosis, and report on the sheep clinical pathologies throughout osteoporosis model development.

pmc-13576361.title: Analysis of risk factors for perioperative hypothermia in patients undergoing spinal trauma surgery
pmc-13576361.creator: Wu Ruimin, Li Yaqiu, Dilinuer Tusentuheti, Yang Sifan, Wu Ruitian
pmc-13576361.description: BackgroundTo investigate the independent risk factors for perioperative hypothermia in patients undergoing spinal trauma surgery, and to provide evidence-based support for developing targeted preventive strategies.MethodsA retrospective cohort study was conducted, including 222 patients who underwent spinal trauma surgery at a single hospital between January 2022 and December 2024.

uslaw-usc-t7-s2255a.title: 7 U.S.C. § 2255a — Financial assistance to national and international conferences
uslaw-usc-t7-s2255a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t7-s2255a.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 55 (Department Of Agriculture). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. On and after October 21, 1993, appropriations available to the Department of Agriculture can be used to provide financial assistance to the organizers of national and international conferences, if such conferences are in support of agency programs.
